correctness.rationale: Exact 65,536-mask enumeration per graph and two equivalent face predicates, checked downward closure, all Hasse incidences verified, acyclic topological sorts visiting 59,819 and 59,747 faces, complete matching critical profiles (one 0 and eleven 9; one 0, one 9 and two 11), and Morse CW theorem prove the integral homotopy/homology. Signed invariant-face Lefschetz sums plus exact Fourier inversion prove the sixteen-value translation character. The rook attaching maps in unstable homotopy are not assumed trivial.

originality.rationale: The complete dominance-complex homotopy of the Shrikhande graph, corresponding rook integral homology, and Shrikhande translation character are not stated or implied by the inspected exact primary results for cycles, forests, chordal graphs, or path strips. The closest public graph-pair records compute different simplicial functors (ordinary independence or metric Čech), and the Shrikhande neighborhood-complex result concerns the original graph, not its complement. Searches covered direct aliases and combinatorial Alexander duality; unindexed prior computations remain possible.
residual_risks: Equivalent unindexed or unpublished domination/closed-neighborhood hypergraph computations could exist.
The comparison does not establish priority over all print books, theses, or inaccessible older sources.

value.rationale: The two uniquely comparable strongly regular (16,6,2,2) graphs form a canonical test for topological invariants beyond regularity parameters. The dominance complex of each is a natural combinatorial Alexander dual tied to domination and coloring; the new complete Shrikhande homotopy, rook contrasting integral homology, and translation character offer precise nontrivial structural information. This is neither a parameter renaming nor a known independence/Čech table recomputation, and no all-graphs theorem is claimed.
